answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance arises by requiring each participant to produce a unique kernel of verifiable work every epoch: a hash chain starting from a public seed that embeds their own recent inference trace. This creates a checkable rule—peers recompute the expected output and reject any mismatch. Attackers incur real costs, as spawning a ripple of fake agents demands running full model passes on dedicated hardware for each identity, far beyond cheap copying, while honest agents sit atop a mesa of shared verification.
